findings.description: Long-lived AWS access keys (access_key/secret_key) are embedded in plaintext Lambda environment variables, which are stored unencrypted in Terraform state and readable by anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration. Credentials should be supplied from Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store via a KMS-encrypted reference instead.

The environment block does not set a kms_key_arn, so Lambda stores the sensitive variables under the default service key rather than a customer-managed key, weakening confidentiality and auditability of the secrets it holds.
runtime is set to nodejs12.x, which is deprecated and no longer receives security patches; known Node.js and dependency vulnerabilities will remain unpatched in the function.

The role's trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume it, but no permissions policies or boundary are defined in this configuration; depending on attached policies this can yield broad access, so the role should be scoped to the specific actions the analytics function requires.
